message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 102, "amount_cents": 2289}, {"order_id": 105, "amount_cents": 33575}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the actual orders and refunds rather than relying only on W2's summary of applied refunds.
Orders show acme, birch, and cobalt. Before paying, I need to check the refund records to confirm W2's claimed refunds (102 and 105) match what is on the ledger.

The refunds ledger matches W2's claim (102 and 105, same amounts), and the orders cover three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 46215 matches its orders (27247 + 18968) with no refunds, so it checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net_cents is 65068, but its orders are 29562 + 35506 = 65068 with no refunds, so it checks out. Next I'll check cobalt, which has both refunds applied.
Cobalt's net of 2634 matches its orders (4653 + 33845 = 38498) minus its refunds (2289 + 33575 = 35864), so all three balances reconcile. I'll record acme's payout of 46215 first.
Acme's payout of 46215 is recorded. Birch's balance of 65068 reconciles with its orders and has no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net of 2634 reconciles with its orders minus refunds, and acme and birch are already recorded. Recording cobalt's payout completes the batch.
All three customers were paid and each recorded payout matched its reconciled balance, so the batch is complete.
